courses.title: Scripting: PowerShell
courses.description: Learn PowerShell from the console to real automation — cmdlets, the object pipeline, scripts, and practical admin tasks.

content.intro: PowerShell is a shell and scripting language built on .NET. Commands are cmdlets in a consistent Verb-Noun form.

p: Windows PowerShell (5.1) ships with Windows; PowerShell 7+ (cross-platform) is a separate install. Run it in the console or VS Code.

sections.code:
Get-Process
Get-Service
Get-Command *service*   # discover commands
Get-Help Get-Process -Examples  # learn any command

note.text: Get-Command finds cmdlets; Get-Help explains them. You rarely need to memorize — you explore.

content.practice: Write the command to find help (with examples) for Get-Service.

quiz.p: To see usage examples for a cmdlet use…

content.intro: PowerShell's superpower: cmdlets pass .NET objects (not text) down the pipeline, so you can filter and shape data precisely.

p: Get-Process returns process objects with properties (Name, CPU, Id). Pipe them to other cmdlets to refine.

sections.code:
Get-Process | Where-Object CPU -gt 100      # filter
Get-Process | Select-Object Name, CPU        # pick columns
Get-Process | Sort-Object CPU -Descending    # order

note.text: Pipe to Get-Member to see an object's properties and methods: Get-Process | Get-Member.

content.practice: Write a pipeline that lists the top 5 processes by CPU, showing only Name and CPU.

quiz.p: The pipeline passes what between cmdlets?
Which filters objects by a condition?
To see an object's properties/methods, pipe to…

content.intro: Store and compare data with variables, arrays, and hashtables.

note.text: PowerShell uses -eq, not == (== is not a PowerShell operator).

content.practice: Declare a hashtable for a server (name + IP) and access the IP.

content.intro: Make decisions and repeat work with conditionals and loops.

note.text: $_ (or $PSItem) is the current object inside Where-Object/ForEach-Object.

content.practice: Write a foreach loop that prints the name of every stopped service.

quiz.p: Inside ForEach-Object, the current item is…
Which handles multiple discrete cases cleanly?

quiz.ex: It runs the block per element.

content.intro: Package reusable logic into functions and save scripts as .ps1 files.

p: Save commands in a .ps1 file and run it. Parameters via param() at the top make scripts reusable.

note.text: Scripts may be blocked by execution policy. Set-ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned (admin) allows local scripts; understand the security trade-off.

content.practice: Write a function with a parameter that returns free space for a given drive.

quiz.p: PowerShell script files use the extension…

content.intro: Put it together: query the system, filter, and export — the essence of admin automation.

sections.code:
# Top 5 CPU consumers to CSV
Get-Process | Sort-Object CPU -Descending |
  Select-Object -First 5 Name, CPU |
  Export-Csv top.csv -NoTypeInformation

# Stopped services
Get-Service | Where-Object Status -eq 'Stopped'

ul: Schedule scripts with Task Scheduler for recurring automation

note.text: Explore with Get-Command/Get-Member, build a one-liner, then save it as a script.

content.practice: Write a one-liner that exports all stopped services to a CSV file.

quiz.ex: Task Scheduler runs scripts on a schedule.

courses.title: Scripting: Python
courses.description: Learn Python for IT: from syntax and data structures to files, errors, and real automation scripts.

content.intro: Python is a readable, general-purpose language. Run it interactively or as .py files.

sections.code:
python --version      # check version
python script.py      # run a file
# interactive REPL:
>>> print('Hello')
Hello

name = 'Ada'
count = 42
print(f'{name} has {count} items')   # f-string

note.text: Python uses indentation (not braces) to define blocks — be consistent (4 spaces).

content.practice: Write a line that prints a name and count using an f-string.

content.intro: Python's built-in types and collections cover most needs.

sections.code:
fruits = ['apple', 'pear']      # list (ordered, mutable)
point = (3, 4)                  # tuple (immutable)
user = {'name': 'Ada', 'age': 36}  # dict (key/value)
unique = {1, 2, 3}              # set (unique)

content.practice: Create a dict for a server (name + ip) and print the ip.

quiz.p: Key/value pairs are stored in a…

quiz.ex: len() gives the number of items.

content.intro: Branch and repeat with if/elif/else and loops.

note.text: break exits a loop; continue skips to the next iteration.

content.practice: Write a for loop that prints numbers 0 through 4.

quiz.p: To skip to the next loop iteration use…
quiz.ex: continue skips to the next iteration.

content.intro: Reuse code with functions and tap the ecosystem with modules.

sections.code:
def disk_free_gb(path='/'):
    import shutil
    return shutil.disk_usage(path).free / 1e9

print(disk_free_gb())

import os, json          # standard library
from datetime import date
# third-party:
pip install requests

note.text: The standard library (os, sys, json, re, datetime) covers a lot before you need pip packages.

content.practice: Define a function with a default parameter that returns a value.

quiz.p: Which is part of Python's standard library?
quiz.ex: json ships with Python; requests is third-party.

content.intro: Read/write files safely and handle errors gracefully.

sections.code:
with open('log.txt') as f:      # auto-closes
    for line in f:
        print(line.strip())

with open('out.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write('done')

note.text: The with statement closes the file automatically, even on error.

content.practice: Write a try/except that converts input to int and handles a bad value.

quiz.p: The safe way to open files is…

content.intro: Automate real tasks: run commands, parse data, and call APIs.

sections.code:
import os, subprocess
os.listdir('.')                     # list files
subprocess.run(['ping', '-c', '1', 'example.com'])

import json, requests
r = requests.get('https://api.example.com/status')
data = r.json()
print(data['state'])

note.text: Read input (files/args/APIs) → transform → output (file/report). Small scripts compound into big time savings.

content.practice: Outline a script that reads a log file and counts lines containing 'ERROR'.

quiz.p: Run an external command from Python with…
Parse a JSON API response with…

quiz.ex: Input → transform → output is the core pattern.
